Since \(f(x)\ge 0\) for all real \(x\) and \(a\ne 0\), we must have \(a>0\). The minimum value occurs at the vertex:
\[
f\left(-\frac b{2a}\right)=c-\frac{b^2}{4a}\ge 0,
\]
so
\[
c\ge \frac{b^2}{4a}.
\]
For fixed \(a,b\), \(M=\frac{a+b+c}{b-a}\) is minimized when \(c=\frac{b^2}{4a}\). Let \(t=\frac ba>1\). Then
\[
M=\frac{a+at+\frac{a t^2}{4}}{at-a}
=\frac{1+t+\frac{t^2}{4}}{t-1}
=\frac{(t+2)^2}{4(t-1)}.
\]
Differentiate:
\[
\frac{d}{dt}\left(\frac{(t+2)^2}{4(t-1)}\right)
=\frac{(t+2)(t-4)}{4(t-1)^2}.
\]
Thus the minimum occurs at \(t=4\), giving
\[
M_{\min}=\frac{(4+2)^2}{4(4-1)}=\frac{36}{12}=3.
\]
\[
\boxed{3}
\]
